author: Amr
subject: fix(styles): move the FAB layer band below the overlay surfaces (#580)
body:
* fix(styles): move the FAB layer band below the overlay surfaces

Every FAB token sat above every overlay: back-to-top 1050, feedback
1051, chat 1052, toc 1055, local-graph 1060 against backdrop 1040,
offcanvas 1045 and modal 1055. With the search modal, the main-nav
offcanvas or the TOC panel open, the TOC and local-graph FABs painted
over it undimmed and `elementFromPoint` at their centres returned the
FAB icons. `fab-toc` tied with `modal` and won on DOM order, because the
FABs render after the footer.

Move the band to 1031-1035 so the scale reads header 1030 < FABs <
backdrop 1040 < offcanvas 1045 < modal 1055 — the ordering the token
file's own header already promised. FABs never overlap the fixed header,
so nothing else moves. The local-graph panel is non-modal and opens over
its own FAB, which is fine: it has its own close button.

- retune the five --zer0-layer-fab-* tokens and the design-system mirror
- retune the stale var() fallbacks in ai-chat.html (1052) and
  _page-feedback.scss (1051), and the numbers quoted in
  docs/architecture/ui-components.md
- add test/visual/features/fab-layer-order.spec.js: a source contract
  asserting every FAB is above the header and strictly below backdrop,
  offcanvas and modal, that the mirror agrees, and that no var()
  fallback re-introduces an above-the-overlay value

Feature: ZER0-081 (design tokens / layer scale)

Fixes #572

The PRD's generated "Feature catalog" block listed the two removed features
as planned, because the hub's governance_lint.py falls back from
`implemented: false` to `planned` when an entry carries no `status:`. Both
keep `implemented: false` and `removed_in:` and now say `status: deprecated`,
which validate-features.rb accepts since #598.

ZER0-088 (zer0 studio) named no PRD requirement. Its token and skin editors
with WCAG contrast and docs-site previews are the browser theme customizer
PRD Feature 13 describes, the requirement ZER0-065 already serves, so it
maps to "Feature 13".

The header now tracks the gem version (1.31.3), which clears the
validator's one warning. The block was regenerated with
`governance_lint.py prd-sync . --write` (hub v2); a second run reports it
unchanged.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): tag the loaded image, not the runner's newest, in test-latest (#619)
body:
TEST (Latest Dependencies) has failed on main since 2026-11-11 (runs
42971426549, 43167200784, 43172175640). The Test Suite job loaded the
artifact, then picked `docker images | head -1`, which on current
ubuntu-latest runners is a preinstalled Agentic Workflow Firewall image
(921e50aed7b2). Validation ran inside that container and its entrypoint
timed out waiting for an iptables init container.

Read the ID from `docker load`'s own output (as the publish job already
did) and fail loudly instead of falling back to the newest image.

body:
* ci(harness): bring the AI workflows onto the fleet harness standard

The five AI workflows now pass every control of the fleet harness
standard (bamr87/bamr87 _data/fleet.yml harnesses.standard).

ai-content-review, ci-self-repair, ui-audit: the bare `claude -p` call is
replaced by the hub's claude-run step with the same prompt, tool list,
model (claude-sonnet-5-5) and turn cap. Each gains a $10 dollar cap, the
credential order from CLAUDE_AUTH_ORDER, usage metering and a kill switch
that defaults on (AI_CONTENT_REVIEW_ENABLED, CI_SELF_REPAIR_ENABLED,
UI_AUDIT_ENABLED). The content-review guard (#418) keeps its own step and
also refuses an answer from the runner's tool-less API fallback.

issue-autopilot: a turn cap on each agent step (triage 20 and verify 20
from the usage ledger, resolve 60 by rule), a timeout on each job that
runs one, and `autopilot:go` starts a run only when the repository owner
applied the label.

visual-evidence-autogen: a turn cap of 30, from the usage ledger.

claude.yml is untouched: the hub's kit-upgrade fan-out owns it.

ai-content-review and ui-audit pass `permission-mode: default` to the

author: Amr
subject: fix(deps): open dependency PRs with FLEET_TOKEN so CI runs (#628)
body:
The weekly gem-update PR was pushed and opened with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
fires no workflows, so #590 and #605 sat with no CI until a maintainer
approved the runs. Checkout and create-pull-request now use FLEET_TOKEN.

A first step probes the token with `gh api user` and fails the job with
an ::error before anything is pushed if the secret is empty or rejected.
There is no GITHUB_TOKEN fallback: it would silently bring back PRs
without CI.

The review request to bamr87 is skipped when FLEET_TOKEN authenticates
as bamr87: GitHub rejects a review request from the PR's own author
(422) and create-pull-request v8 rethrows it, failing the run after the
PR is already open.

Co-authored-by: bamr87 <bamr87@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: feat(audit-consumer): detect stale vendored theme _data (#629)
body:
* test(audit): read assertion output from a here-string

`echo "$actual" | grep -qF` under `set -o pipefail` races: grep -q exits on
the first match and closes the pipe, echo dies of SIGPIPE when the match
comes before the end of a large output (the 56 KB manifest), and the
pipeline reads as failed. On unmodified main the section-1 manifest
assertions failed at random in a Linux container (24-25 of 31 passed over
three runs); with a here-string the suite is a stable 29 of 31, the two
remaining failures being the known release-snapshot and fixture ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(audit-consumer): detect stale vendored theme _data

Jekyll 3.10 (GitHub Pages) never loads a theme's _data/, so a consumer
reads the theme's data only from its own copy, which does not float with
remote_theme. audit-consumer scanned only themable_paths, so a copy that
fell behind a theme data fix (#240's dark/contrast skins) went unreported.

- scripts/lib/audit.sh keeps the theme-owned registries a consumer copies
  verbatim (_data/theme_skins.yml, _data/theme_backgrounds.yml).
  scripts/bin/manifest publishes them as vendored_data_paths and checksums
  them with the themable files; _data/theme-manifest.yml is left to the
  release flow (manifest-sync.yml).
- audit-consumer classifies each as IDENTICAL, STALE (differs, not declared
  in .theme-overrides.yml), DIFFERS_JUSTIFIED or MISSING, falling back to
  the built-in list when the manifest predates the key. STA…

* feat(layouts): keep admin actions reachable on mobile and group the admin sidebar

The admin_actions buttons sat in a d-none d-md-flex wrapper, so below
768px no header action rendered. The first action is now a button at
every width and any others open from a "More actions" dropdown; the
title row wraps so the actions take their own line on a phone.

render as before. Counts are plain numerals, statuses a dot plus a word,
and the active item a skin tint with aria-current instead of the solid
primary pill (_sass/layouts/_admin.scss). The desktop sidebar's
"Administration" h6 is removed, leaving the offcanvas title as the one
heading. The sticky-offset clause of T-041 moves to T-039.

Refs: T-041
Closes #409

author: Amr
subject: feat(includes): configurable giscus theme, mapping and language (#634)
body:
content/giscus.html hard-coded data-theme="preferred_color_scheme", so the
widget followed the visitor's OS rather than the site: a dark-skin site
showed a white comment box to every visitor in light mode, and the only
fix was to fork the include. data-mapping, data-input-position and
data-lang were fixed the same way.

Each now reads site.giscus.<attribute> (the hyphenated style of the
existing keys) and falls back to its old value, so a site that sets none
of the keys renders the same tag byte for byte. Values are HTML-escaped.

content/comments.html now owns the comment section of every layout that
has one: the site.giscus.enabled gate, the page.comments default
(default_on), the heading and the widget. article, note and notebook stay
on unless a page sets comments: false; recipe and book-story stay opt-in
(comments: true); note and notebook keep their div/h5 form (compact). A
consumer layout needs one include line.

test/test_giscus_config.rb builds throwaway sites through the real layouts
and runs in test_core.sh as "Giscus Config Overlay"; the static giscus
check now follows the wrapper.

Closes #574

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

table of contents the theme does not have: a Kramdown `toc_only` filter, a

- the three files involved (default.html, navigation/sidebar-right.html and

- troubleshooting steps that point at the real gates

Heading Levels and Scoping the TOC to the Body were already correct and are
unchanged. fr/docs/features/toc.md is generated by translate.yml and is left
for its next run.

body:
* fix(deps): re-lock github-pages 233 to lift rubyzip to 3.7.0 (GHSA-47m2-wp7j-p9vc)

github-pages 232 pinned jekyll-remote-theme 0.4.3, which capped rubyzip
below 3.0 and held the lock on the vulnerable rubyzip 2.4.1 (Dependabot
alert #64, high, < 3.4.0). github-pages 233 pins jekyll-remote-theme 0.6.2
(rubyzip < 4.0), so `bundle lock --update github-pages rubyzip` now resolves
rubyzip 3.7.0. Gemfile already admits 233; no pin added.

Drop the bundler block from .github/dependabot.yml: it existed only to carry
the rubyzip >= 3.0 ignore, whose stated removal condition (a github-pages
release whose remote-theme allows rubyzip 3.x) is now met.

Closes #594

author: Amr
subject: ci(claude): use OAuth only, disable API key for now (#627)
body:
Remove every use of the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret from the workflows so
Claude runs on CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN only. Gates that accepted "OAuth
or key" now require OAuth, and the "OAuth wins" unset blocks drop the key
unconditionally (failing clearly without a token).

deploy-chat-proxy no longer uploads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to the Cloudflare
Worker (the Worker calls the Anthropic API directly); it still deploys
code, and the Worker keeps whatever credential Cloudflare already holds.

The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret itself is untouched; to restore, revert.

* feat(includes): render the footer newsletter form only with a provider

Every page of every site rendered a newsletter form that could not be
used: a disabled email input, a disabled "Subscribe" button whose
tooltip was a setup note, and a "placeholder until you connect a
provider" caption. No config key enabled it or hid it.

The footer now resolves a top-level `newsletter:` block, falling back
to `news.newsletter:` (the news band's block), and renders the form
only when it has a non-blank `endpoint` and is not `enabled: false`.

enabled, required email input and a submit button; its strings come
from four new ui-text keys. Without a form the policy links take the
whole row, centred. There is no mailto: fallback.

body:

TEST (Latest Dependencies) has failed on main since 2026-11-11 (runs
42971426549, 43167200784, 43172175640). The Test Suite job loaded the
artifact, then picked `docker images | head -1`, which on current
